subject: Multi-tenant index transfer playbook — initial alignment with NimbusDB
messages:
From: Alex Smith <alex.smith@nimbusdb.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Index transfer playbook and multi-tenant constraints

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for taking time to talk yesterday. NimbusDB has a handful of customers evaluating a managed vector product where the customer wants their existing pgvector or S3-based indexes migrated into a Nimbus-managed Pinecone-like namespace temporarily for indexing/re-query workloads. The ask is to build a safe, repeatable playbook for:

- exporting vectors and metadata from pgvector (Postgres) or S3 chunk+manifest stores;
- verifying dimensionality and tokenizer alignment;
- performing zero-downtime transfer into a Nimbus-managed index; and
- secure rollback / deletion policies tied to customer contracts.

Key constraints to flag up-front:
- Some customers require data to never leave their VPC (so either Redwood Private or a signed S3 transfer is needed).
- KMS + audit log requirements for any persisted transfer.
- They expect a short RTO if the managed index becomes unavailable.

Can you and your team map out the technical steps and commercial guardrails (SLA, liability, who stores backups) so we can present a joint offering to three pilot customers next month? I attached an initial checklist we use internally.

Proposed next steps: 1) alignment call w/ engineers, 2) scoped pilot statement of work, 3) shared migration runbook.

Cheers,
Alex

--
Alex Smith
Head of Partner Engineering, NimbusDB
alex.smith@nimbusdb.com
+1 (415) 555-0199
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Alex Smith <alex.smith@nimbusdb.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Index transfer playbook and multi-tenant constraints

Alex — thanks for the clear write-up and the checklist, this is actionable. Attaching a small migration checklist we've used for dedicated customers; it includes export patterns (pg_dump + vector export script), S3 manifest schema, and a validation checklist.

High-level answers up-front:
- Data residency / VPC: we can run Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane) or support a signed, ephemeral S3 transfer orchestration so data never lands in Nimbus-managed storage. Recommend the Private route for customers with strict residency.
- KMS / audit logs: Redwood can require customer KMS keys for any export artifacts and we can surface audit logs back to the customer console. We'll need Nimbus to support accepting encrypted manifests and provide a key exchange procedure.
- RTO / rollback: we propose a dual-write window for 48 hours and a cold fallback path to the source index. If Nimbus exposes a snapshot API, rollbacks can be automated.

Suggested agenda for the alignment call (30 min):
1) Tech owners: data export formats (Ben)
2) Security: KMS + attestations (Vanessa)
3) Ops: snapshot/rollback SLA (Connor)
4) Commercial: liability and data retention (we can loop in legal after technical alignment)

Can Ben and Vanessa join a quick call Monday at 10am PT? Also Alex, can you confirm the three pilot customers' approximate data sizes (GB of vectors) and whether any are air-gapped?

Attachments: index-migration-checklist.xlsx (see export/validate tabs)

Thanks,
Connor

--
Connor O'Brien
Partner Lead, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Nimbus pilot prep — internal checklist and owners

Folks — looping you in after Nimbus' ask. Short internal notes / owners before Monday's sync: 

1) Export formats (owner: Ben)
- Confirm pgvector export tooling: provide SQL snippet + vector-dump utility that preserves dims and metadata.
- S3 manifests: define schema (object key, chunk id, metadata json, tokenizer version).

2) Security controls (owner: Vanessa)
- KMS key exchange procedure: support customer-supplied KMS; outline how Nimbus will request ephemeral decryption tokens and how audits are logged.
- For Private deployments: checklist for network peering and host-level hardening.

3) Operational runbook (owner: Marissa)
- Dual-write window plan: how long, metrics to monitor, rollback triggers (missed heartbeats, QC fail rate > 2%).
- Snapshot/retention: define retention default of 30 days for pilot, encrypted at rest.

4) Commercial guardrails (I'll own initial legal loop)
- Suggested SLA: 99.5% index availability during pilot with predefined remediation credits.
- Data retention liability: who is responsible for leftover snapshots after pilot termination?

Please review the attached draft checklist and add comments directly in the Drive link. We'll consolidate and send Nimbus a 1-page runbook after the Monday meeting.

Connor

Connor / team — appreciate the fast turnaround and the internal owners. Confirming the call Monday at 10am PT. Answers to the sizing / customer notes you asked for: 

- Pilot A: 120GB vectors (pgvector), not air-gapped.
- Pilot B: 18GB vectors stored as S3 chunks, requires data to remain in EU region (we'll need to scope region-specific flow for that one).
- Pilot C: 5GB, air-gapped customer with strict KMS controls — they'll require use of Redwood Private or a signed S3 transfer.

Attachments included: nimbus-data-flow-diagram.png, nimbus-sla-proposal.pdf. Also shared a HubSpot deal (NIM-2027-304) with the named pilots and initial commercial terms.

One note on rollback: Nimbus can export on-demand snapshots, but to automate rollback we will need the snapshot retention to be 72 hours and a documented API endpoint to trigger a restore — can your ops/Marissa confirm if that is feasible?

Forwarding our standard partner migration agreement in DocuSign; sign when you have legal alignment and we'll slot the pilot.

Thanks,
Alex
